title: RCMP probe death of man in custody
article: A Nelson House man complained about feeling ill just hours before dying in RCMP custody last week.

Nisichawayasihk Chief Jim Moore said the 42-year-old man, who was rushed to the local nursing station after being found unresponsive in a holding cell in the RCMP detachment Thursday, had already gone to the nursing station on Wednesday night.
"He was at the nursing station for something he was complaining about," Moore said on Friday. "He was eventually released.
"I think there was a history of medical problems with this person... he was diabetic... we're all on edge waiting for the autopsy report.
The man, who has not been identified, was pronounced dead after being rushed to the nursing station. CPR was performed, but was unsuccessful.

The death comes just seven months after a provincial court judge released a report saying RCMP at Norway House didn't follow their own policies and didn't immediately rush Sherrill Forbister to hospital in October 2003.
An autopsy found Forbister would have lived had he been taken to hospital while he was still breathing and with a pulse.

Instead of officers rushing Forbister to hospital, when they found him passed out inside a home with fresh blood near his eye, they headed to their detachment. The officers called for an ambulance when they discovered Forbister wasn't breathing when they took him out of their cruiser.
RCMP Sgt. Line Karpish said an autopsy was being performed on the Nisichawayasihk man in Winnipeg at the Health Sciences Centre on Friday.
RCMP said the deceased man's family and the Nelson House chief and council are being kept up-to-date about the RCMP investigation.
